prompt: I ran Louvain community detection on my co-authorship network (1200 authors, 4800 edges) and got 8 communities. The modularity is 0.67 which seems great. How do I report these communities in my paper? I want to name them and describe what each one represents.
expectations: Output warns that a single Louvain run reflects modularity DEGENERACY — many qualitatively different partitions have near-equal modularity (Good et al.) — not just random stochasticity
Output frames stability analysis as a PREREQUISITE before naming or interpreting communities, not as an optional improvement step
Output recommends running community detection many times (e.g., 100+ runs) and measuring pairwise stability with ARI, NMI, or similar
Output recommends comparing Q = 0.67 against a configuration-model null (random graphs with the same degree sequence) rather than accepting it at face value
Output mentions Louvain resolution limit or the alternative of SBM (Stochastic Block Model) for more principled partitioning
